newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says Moodys too worried by external debt.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says Moodys too worried by external debt.

text.p: Moody's Investor Services gives too much weight to external debt in its credit rating of Argentina, Carlos Rodriguez, the Economy Minister's chief advisor, said Wednesday.
"Moody's puts an exaggerated weight on external debt," Rodriguez told journalists. "I am totally convinced."

Rodriguez made the statements after Standard & Poor's announced Tuesday that it removed the sovereign ratings ceiling on Argentine corporations and upgraded the ratings on several of them to investment grade status.
"It is a good indicator for Argentina that they (S&P) have raised Argentine companies to investment-grade," he said.
In March, S&P also raised the long-term sovereign foreign currency rating on Argentina to BB from BB-. It said Tuesday's move was unrelated to that upgrade.
"I think Moody's exaggerates the issue (foreign debt) and S&P has a much more clear picture of it," added Rodriguez.
He said Moody's only pointed to the external debt of firms, but did not count in the assets in foreign currencies also held by those companies.
All the same, the S&P upgrade of firms led Rodriguez to conclude: "This shows that there is a lot to do at the government level."

"What are we missing? There is a lot of debt and I think we have to reduce it and there are two ways to do that: generate a flow of funds or sell assets," he said, urging the government to make efforts in reducing debt levels.
Using proceeds from privatizations to pay off debt, or running a budget surplus, would be ways to cut the debt, said Rodriguez.
